theater: 河南洛陽孟津河陰渡口

battle.name: 河陰之戰
battle.theater: 河南洛陽孟津河陰渡口
battle.brief: 北周建德四年（575）七月至九月，周武帝宇文邕統軍十餘萬東伐北齊，八月二十四日陷河陰、武濟、洛口，焚黃河浮橋，圍中潬城二十餘日；九月齊援軍自晉陽抵河陽，周軍遂棄三十餘城班師。卡面的羅馬重步兵不屬於本役，其位置對應的是周齊雙方的重裝步兵與北齊甲騎。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 北周與北齊在河陰一線的對峙，是南北朝末年兩個北方政權在黃河中游的總決戰前哨。北周方面，軍令出自皇帝周武帝宇文邕本人；其兵制承自西魏宇文泰所創的府兵與柱國大將軍體制，以八柱國十二大將軍分統各部，漢人與鮮卑人組成的軍隊混編為旅，兵農合一，平時屯田、戰時徵發，宿衛與京師禁軍另立一軍。宇文邕在建德二年除掉專權的宇文護後親掌軍政，數年北伐已收復汾北、晉陽一線；此役他自將大軍十餘萬出關中，兵分六路同時壓向河陰、黎陽與河北內地，樞機與總管之職由宇文純、司馬消難、達奚震、宇文盛、侯莫陳崇、宇文招分擔，隋公楊堅另領水軍三萬自渭河入黃河，申公李穆守河陽道，梁公侯莫陳芮率兩萬截斷並州、冀州、殷州、定州之間的聯絡，常山公于翼屯陳州、汝州防備陳軍。糧秣主力靠關中屯田所出，經渭河、黃河轉運出川。北齊方面，兵權分掌於右丞相高阿那肱、洛州刺史獨孤永業等將門之手，核心是並州晉陽的精騎與河北各道的州兵，後主蕭緯在位時和士開、祖珽等嬖倖用事，政令與軍資多滯，軍人久欠糧餉而將領各自擁兵自重，防守全靠城壘之堅與援軍之速。
countriesEn: The confrontation along the Heyin line was the forward post of the final northern decision between the two northern states of the late Southern and Northern Dynasties, fought in the middle reaches of the Yellow River. On the Zhou side the orders came from the emperor himself, Zhou Wudi, Yuwen Yong. The army rested on the fubing system and on the command structure of pillar lords and generals created by Yuwen Tai of Western Wei: eight pillar lords and twelve generals each led a component, the Han and Xianbei soldiers being mixed into the same units, soldiers and farmers fused so that they lived on the land in peace and were mustered for war, while the guards of the capital formed a command of their own. After killing the regent Yuwen Hu in the second year of Jiande, Yuwen Yong took the military into his own hands, and his northern expeditions in the preceding years had already recovered the Fenbei and Jinyang line. In this campaign he led more than a hundred thousand men out of Guanzhong and pressed on Heyin, Liyang and the northern interior along six separate roads at once. The posts of command were distributed among Yuwen Chun, Sima Xiaonan, Daxi Zhen, Yuwen Sheng, Houmo Chen Chong and Yuwen Zhao, who led the first three armies and the last three armies; Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, took a fleet of thirty thousand that entered the Yellow River from the Wei River; Li Mu, Duke of Shen, held the Heyang road; Houmo Chen Rui led twenty thousand men to cut the links among Bing, Ji, Yin and Ding; and Yu Yi, Duke of Changshan, sat in the prefectures of Chen and Ru watching the Chen army. Grain came chiefly from the military farms of Guanzhong and was moved out of the basin by the Wei and Yellow Rivers. On the Qi side command was shared among the right chancellor Gao Anahong, the governor of Luozhou Dugu Yongye and other generals, and its core was the elite cavalry of Jinyang in Bingzhou together with the prefectural troops of the Hebei circuits. Under the last emperor, Xiao Wei, the favourites He Shikai and Zu Ting monopolised affairs; government orders and military funds jammed, soldiers had long gone without pay and rations, and generals held private forces of their own, so that the defence rested entirely on the strength of the walls and the speed of the relieving armies.
people: 留下姓名的，多半可以在北周一方找到。發動整場戰役的周武帝宇文邕，是唯一有權決定進退的人：他採納了驃騎大將軍韋孝寬的東伐之策，親率主力出關中；屯軍金墉、中潬城下時他患病，班師與否亦出在他手。韋孝寬是此策的首倡者，他此前已北伐至燕、汾，屢克城池，守玉壁時以少量守兵頂住高長恭大軍而名震北方，料定齊人新敗、人心思亂，此時用兵正是時機。齊王宇文憲領兵兩萬屯黎陽，攻取武濟與洛口兩城並焚毀黃河浮橋，是切斷洛陽與河北聯繫的關鍵一擊；隋公楊堅領水軍三萬由渭河入黃河，掌運道與側翼，這是他以水軍身分第一次獨當一面，日後代周建隋亦由此起步。梁公侯莫陳芮、申公李穆、常山公于翼分斷河北交通與陳州方向，滎陽公司馬消難、鄭公達奚震與越王宇文盛、周昌公侯莫陳崇、趙王宇文招分任前後三軍總管。北齊一方，右丞相高阿那肱自晉陽率援軍南下抵河陽，洛州刺史獨孤永業守金墉城而未被攻破，傅伏屯中潬城力抗周軍圍攻；齊後主蕭緯遠在鄴城，朝廷的和士開、祖珽等人只知斂財自固，未能作出有效調度。同期南方的陳宣帝正以吳明徹等將北伐，奪取江北、淮南，使齊軍不能全力西向。
peopleEn: The names that survive are mostly on the Zhou side. The man who set the whole war in motion was Zhou Wudi, Yuwen Yong, the only person with the authority to decide whether the host advanced or withdrew: he took up the proposal for an eastern campaign made by the commander of the cavalry, Wei Xiaokuan, and led the main army out of Guanzhong in person; when the army sat before Jinyong and Zhongtan he fell ill, and the decision to break off was likewise his. Wei Xiaokuan was the author of the plan, having already campaigned north to Yan and Fen, taken city after city, and made his name in the north by holding Yubi with a handful of men against the army of Gao Changgong; he judged that Qi, freshly beaten and unsettled, was at that moment the moment to strike. The Prince of Qi, Yuwen Xian, led twenty thousand men to Liyang, took Wuji and the two cities of Luokou and burned the floating bridge over the Yellow River, and this was the blow that cut Luoyang off from the north. Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, led thirty thousand men in the fleet that came down the Wei into the Yellow River, holding the supply route and the northern flank; this was the first command of his own he had ever held, and it was here that the road to his later usurpation of Zhou and foundation of the Sui began. The Duke of Liang, Houmo Chen Rui, the Duke of Shen, Li Mu, and the Duke of Changshan, Yu Yi, were set to cut the northern roads and to cover the Chen-Ru sector; the Duke of Yingyang, Sima Xiaonan, the Duke of Zheng, Daxi Zhen, the Prince of Yue, Yuwen Sheng, the Duke of Zhouchang, Houmo Chen Chong, and the Prince of Zhao, Yuwen Zhao, served as commanders of the first three armies and the last three armies. On the Qi side the right chancellor Gao Anahong marched the relieving army down from Jinyang to Heyang; the governor of Luozhou, Dugu Yongye, held Jinyong city and was not taken; Fu Fu stood at Zhongtan and resisted the Zhou siege. The last emperor of Qi, Xiao Wei, sat far away at Ye, and at court He Shikai and Zu Ting thought only of amassing wealth for themselves, without producing any effective direction. At the same moment the Chen emperor Xuan was campaigning north with generals such as Wu Mingche, taking the lands north of the river and south of the Huai, which prevented the Qi army from concentrating to the west.
kits: 卡面上的羅馬重步兵並未出現在河陰戰場：北周與北齊的戰士屬於東亞的軍隊體系，與地中海世界的羅馬兵制並無交集，所以本役的兵器記載只能說明卡面所屬的兵種譜系，而不涉及其實戰使用。卡面這件裝備的意義在於它是重裝步兵的原型——分段鎧甲配大盾，靠徵兵與補給撐住陣線，而不是靠裝備本身取勝。北周軍中與之功能相近的是披明光鎧、持長槊與大盾的重裝步兵，編在鋒線與攻城序列的末端，用來在正面吸住敵軍的衝鋒，掩護後方弩手與騎兵展開；北齊與之對應的是重裝步騎與所謂的甲騎，以及精於騎射的並州騎兵，在晉陽與河陽之間奔馳求戰。實際交戰中可確定的裝備有：周軍的長槊、角弓、弩、鎧甲與兜鍪，攻城所用的雲梯、撞車與攻城塔，楊堅水軍的舟船與浮筏，以及用來切斷洛陽北向聯繫的黃河浮橋；齊軍則有城樓、壘柵、拒馬與守城弓弩。值得一記的是周武帝入齊境後所下的禁令：軍士不得伐樹、踐踏莊稼，違者嚴懲——這條軍紀本身說明進軍季節正當農時，糧食供應倚賴未受蹂躪的莊稼與河運。
kitsEn: The Roman heavy infantry on the card never appeared on the battlefield of Heyin: the soldiers of Northern Zhou and Northern Qi belonged to the East Asian military world and had nothing in common with the Roman system of the Mediterranean, so the arms recorded for this campaign can only identify the lineage to which the card belongs and cannot speak of its actual use in the fighting. The significance of the card's item is that it is the archetype of the heavy infantryman: segmentata armour with a heavy shield, holding the line by means of conscription and supply rather than by the quality of the equipment. The closest functional counterpart in the Zhou army was the heavy infantryman in bright armour carrying a long spear and a large shield, placed at the end of the assault and siege columns, used to absorb the enemy's charge in front while the crossbowmen and cavalry opened out behind. On the Qi side the equivalents were the armoured foot and horse, the so-called armoured cavalry, together with the riders of Bingzhou, who were masters of the bow and sought battle between Jinyang and Heyang. The equipment that can actually be confirmed in the fighting includes the long spears, plain bows, crossbows, armour and helmets of the Zhou, the scaling ladders, battering rams and siege towers used in assaults, the boats and pontoons of Yang Jian's fleet, and the floating bridge over the Yellow River by which the road north from Luoyang was cut. The Qi side had wall towers, stockades, chevaux-de-frise and the bows of the garrison. One order deserves to be recorded: when the Zhou army entered Qi territory, Emperor Wu forbade the soldiers to cut trees or trample the crops and punished offenders severely. That rule itself shows the season of the advance fell in the farming months, and that the food supply depended on crops left undamaged and on the river transport.
tactics: 這場戰役的戰術骨架，是多路分進與分割對手的配合。北周沒有把十餘萬人壓成一條攻擊線：主力六萬在周武帝帶領下直取河陰；宇文憲部兩萬在黎陽方向展開，負責攻取洛口、斷浮橋，切斷洛陽與河北的陸路；侯莫陳芮部兩萬深入河北，切斷並州、冀州、殷州、定州之間的往來，使齊軍無法自北面調兵；李穆部三萬守河陽道，控制洛陽通往黃河北岸的通道；楊堅部水軍三萬由渭河入黃河，沿黃河轉運糧秣並監視北岸；于翼部兩萬在陳州、汝州方向警戒陳軍，掩護全軍側翼。進攻有明確次序：八月二十一日大軍入齊境，先以禁令維護沿途莊稼以維持糧源；八月二十四日同一天內攻下河陰、攻克武濟、又取洛口東西二城並焚毀黃河浮橋，兩日之間切斷洛陽對岸的交通節點；其後主力轉攻河陽南城，圍中潬城二十餘日，一面攻城一面阻援。北齊的戰術是純粹的守城待援：以金墉城、中潬城、河陽南城三處城壘拖住周軍，把希望寄在晉陽的援軍上。九月高阿那肱大軍抵達河陽，加上周武帝病勢，北周才放棄所取三十餘城撤回，這是一次因外援已至與主帥病勢而中止的攻勢。
tacticsEn: The tactical skeleton of the campaign was the combination of advance along several roads and the cutting of the enemy's communications. Northern Zhou did not compress more than a hundred thousand men into a single line of attack. Sixty thousand under the emperor drove straight at Heyin. Yuwen Xian's twenty thousand worked out on the Liyang flank, taking Luokou and burning the floating bridge to cut the land road between Luoyang and the north. Houmo Chen Rui's twenty thousand pushed deep into Hebei and cut the traffic among Bing, Ji, Yin and Ding, so that the Qi army could not be shifted from the north. Li Mu's thirty thousand held the Heyang road and controlled the route from Luoyang to the north bank of the Yellow River. Yang Jian's fleet of thirty thousand came down the Wei into the Yellow River, carrying grain along the water and watching the opposite bank. Yu Yi's twenty thousand in the Chen and Ru prefectures watched for the Chen army and covered the flank of the entire host. The attack followed a clear order. On the twenty-first day of the eighth month the army entered Qi territory, and the ban on damaging the crops was issued first, to keep the grain supply in the country. On the twenty-fourth day of the same month Heyin fell, Wuji was taken, the east and west cities of Luokou were carried and the floating bridge over the Yellow River burned, so that within two days the traffic node north of Luoyang was severed. The main force then turned on the south city of Heyang and beleaguered Zhongtan for more than twenty days, besieging and interdicting the relieving army at the same time. The Qi tactics were pure defence and wait for relief: three walled posts, Jinyong, Zhongtan and the south city of Heyang, were used to hold the Zhou army, with all their hopes set on the relieving force from Jinyang. In the ninth month Gao Anahong's host reached Heyang, and with the emperor also taken ill, Zhou gave up the more than thirty places it had won and withdrew. It was an offensive halted by the arrival of relief and by the sickness of the commander-in-chief.
data: 可核的數字不多，但幾個量級相當清楚。周武帝自統大軍「十餘萬」出關中，其中主力六萬分作六路：柱國宇文純、滎陽公司馬消難、鄭公達奚震任前三軍總管，越王宇文盛、周昌公侯莫陳崇、趙王宇文招任後三軍總管；此外齊王宇文憲部兩萬屯黎陽，隋公楊堅部水軍三萬自渭河入黃河，梁公侯莫陳芮部兩萬斷河北四州聯繫，申公李穆部三萬守河陽道，常山公于翼部兩萬在陳州、汝州戒備陳軍，合計與「十餘萬」的說法相去不遠。時間上，七月出兵，八月二十一日入齊境，八月二十四日連下河陰、武濟、洛口三處並焚浮橋，圍中潬城二十餘日，九月高阿那肱自晉陽率軍抵河陽，周軍隨即班師。地理上，河陰在今洛陽孟津，屬黃河北岸的渡口，西距洛口（今鞏義東北）數十里，東北至晉陽（今太原）約四百里，齊援軍正是沿這條晉陽至河陽的線南下。收穫方面可確定的只有據點數目：周軍放棄了三十餘城。兩軍的斬獲數字與耗糧數字在《資治通鑑》等史籍中並無記載，不可代為推算；史家記載此役多用「十餘萬」「二萬」「三萬」「二十餘日」這類概數，本身也說明戰報多靠約數流傳。
dataEn: The verifiable numbers are few, but a few orders of magnitude are quite clear. Zhou Wudi led a host of more than a hundred thousand out of Guanzhong, of which sixty thousand formed the main force in six columns: the pillar lord Yuwen Chun, the Duke of Yingyang Sima Xiaonan and the Duke of Zheng Daxi Zhen as commanders of the first three armies, and the Prince of Yue Yuwen Sheng, the Duke of Zhouchang Houmo Chen Chong and the Prince of Zhao Yuwen Zhao as commanders of the last three. In addition the Prince of Qi, Yuwen Xian, held twenty thousand at Liyang; Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, took thirty thousand in the fleet that came from the Wei into the Yellow River; Houmo Chen Rui took twenty thousand to cut the four northern prefectures off from one another; Li Mu, Duke of Shen, held the Heyang road with thirty thousand; and Yu Yi, Duke of Changshan, guarded the Chen and Ru prefectures with twenty thousand. The total is not far from the figure of more than a hundred thousand. In time: the army set out in the seventh month; on the twenty-first day of the eighth month it entered Qi territory; on the twenty-fourth day of the same month Heyin, Wuji and Luokou fell and the floating bridge was burned; Zhongtan was besieged for more than twenty days; in the ninth month Gao Anahong marched from Jinyang to Heyang, and the Zhou army then withdrew. In geography: Heyin lies in today's Mengjin district of Luoyang, a ford on the north bank of the Yellow River, a few tens of li west of Luokou, now north-east of Gongyi, and about four hundred li south-west of Jinyang, now Taiyuan; the relief army came south along exactly that Jinyang-Heyang line. The only ascertainable result is a count of posts: the Zhou army abandoned more than thirty towns. Figures for casualties and for grain consumed are not recorded in the Zizhi Tongjian or elsewhere and must not be supplied by inference; the historians themselves wrote of this campaign in round numbers such as more than a hundred thousand, twenty thousand, thirty thousand and more than twenty days, which shows how much of the report travelled as approximation.
cause: 起兵的緣由有三層。表層是北齊的南線先被撕開：陳宣帝在太建年間命吳明徹等將北伐，一度取江北、淮南之地，北齊的黃河以南防務因而空虛，河北兵力被抽調南顧。中層是北齊內部的失序：後主蕭緯寵信和士開、祖珽，軍國大事屢被擾動，州郡將領各自擁兵，軍糧久欠，北齊雖增修防禦，卻是有城無人、有兵無糧。深層是北周自身的轉折：宇文邕在建德二年誅宇文護、收回兵權，隨後整軍經武，於建德三年攻取晉陽與汾北諸地，已經打通由山西南下河北的門戶；此時驃騎大將軍韋孝寬進策東伐，周武帝從之，於是建德四年夏秋傾國東出。戰略上還有一層算計：北周用兵正趕在陳軍仍在江北、齊軍南北兩端不能兼顧的窗口，兩面夾擊的格局因此形成，齊人雖增兵設防，卻始終無法集中兵力。
causeEn: There were three layers of reason for the war. On the surface, the southern front of Northern Qi had been torn open first: the Chen emperor Xuan had ordered generals such as Wu Mingche to campaign north in the Taijian years, taking the lands north of the river and south of the Huai, so that Qi's defence below the Yellow River was left hollow and troops were drawn from Hebei to guard the south. Beneath that lay the disorder inside Northern Qi. The last emperor, Xiao Wei, favoured He Shikai and Zu Ting, the business of state was repeatedly thrown into confusion, the commanders of the prefectures held private forces, and the army had long gone without grain; Qi added to its defences, but it had walls without men and soldiers without rations. Deeper still lay a turning point in Northern Zhou. Yuwen Yong killed Yuwen Hu in the second year of Jiande and took back the military authority, then reorganised the troops and put the army through its exercises; in the third year of Jiande he took Jinyang and the places in Fenbei, opening the door that led from Shanxi down into Hebei. At this moment the commander of the cavalry, Wei Xiaokuan, proposed the eastern campaign, and Zhou Wudi accepted it, so that in the summer and autumn of the fourth year of Jiande the whole state moved east. There was a strategic calculation as well: Zhou struck while the Chen army was still north of the river and Qi could not attend to both ends of its front, and the two-sided pincer thus took shape, so that Qi, even though it reinforced and fortified, could never concentrate its troops.
impact: 河陰之役本身沒有攻下洛陽，卻是北周滅齊的第一塊踏板。建德五年周軍再出，韋孝寬攻克晉陽；次年宇文憲大軍直下，鄴城一下，北齊亡國，降兵降將盡為北周、隨後的隋朝所收，北方重新統一。河陰這一役奠定的兩樣東西延續更久：一是進攻方向與補給路線，渭河至黃河的水運自此成為關中輸糧出川的主通道，直至隋唐仍被倚重；二是河津渡口作為南北樞紐的地位，同一片渡口在西魏末年還曾是「河陰之變」的集兵地，說明此處在南北朝政治與軍事上的份量。戰術層面，六路大軍齊發、水陸並進、軍中用明令保障沿途莊稼的做法，顯示這一代戰爭在協同與後勤上的水準已高於此前的中原戰役，而重裝步兵在其中的位置也再次說明：真正的支柱不是甲胄，而是兵源與糧道。往後的連鎖更長——建德七年周武帝病崩，繼位的宇文閔很快被廢，581年楊堅代周建隋，589年隋滅陳，二十餘年間三國盡歸一統；河陰是這條連鎖的第一環。
impactEn: The battle of Heyin did not take Luoyang, but it was the first stepping-stone of Zhou's destruction of Qi. The Zhou army went out again in the fifth year of Jiande and Wei Xiaokuan took Jinyang; the following year Yuwen Xian's host came straight down and Ye fell, Northern Qi was destroyed, and the surrendered soldiers and generals were taken over in full by Northern Zhou and then by the Sui, reunifying the north. Two things fixed by the campaign at Heyin lasted longer than the fighting itself. The first was the direction of advance and the supply route: the water route from the Wei to the Yellow River became the main artery carrying grain out of Guanzhong, and was relied on down through the Sui and Tang. The second was the standing of the river crossing as the hinge between north and south: the same ford had been the mustering place of the so-called Change at Heyin in the last years of Western Wei, which shows what weight this spot carried in the politics and the warfare of the age. On the level of tactics, the deployment of six columns at once, the advance of land and water in step, and the explicit order in the army protecting the crops along the route show a level of coordination and supply in the warfare of this generation that stood above the earlier battles of the Central Plains; and the place of the heavy infantry within it demonstrated once more that the true pillar is not the armour but the men and the grain road. The chain that followed was longer still: Zhou Wudi died of illness in the seventh year of Jiande, his successor Yuwen Min was quickly discarded, Yang Jian replaced Zhou and founded the Sui in 581, and the Sui destroyed Chen in 589, so that within a little more than twenty years the three states were gathered into one. Heyin was the first link in that chain.
result: 這一役的結局是一場未竟的攻勢。八月二十四日周軍連陷河陰、武濟與洛口兩城，焚毀黃河浮橋，一度切斷洛陽與河北的聯繫；但河陽南城與中潬城的圍攻拖了二十餘日，獨孤永業守的金墉城始終未能攻下，九月高阿那肱自晉陽率援軍抵達河陽，而周武帝又正患病，北周遂放棄已攻下的三十餘城，班師回朝，戰果只停在河陽與洛口一線的據點上。對北齊而言，這是致命而及時的一擊：洛口浮橋被毀，黃河渡口為周軍所控，河北與洛陽之間的聯繫被切斷數月，齊軍不得不把主力從晉陽抽調南援；對北周而言，雖然沒有拿下洛陽，卻驗證了多路分進、水陸聯運可以壓住齊軍的城防體系，也讓周武帝看見了北伐可行。兩年後鄴城下的決戰才是真正的結局，但那場戰爭的入口，正是建德四年秋天的河陰。
resultEn: The outcome was an offensive left unfinished. On the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month the Zhou army took Heyin and Wuji and the two cities of Luokou and burned the floating bridge over the Yellow River, severing for a time the link between Luoyang and the north. But the siege of the south city of Heyang and of Zhongtan dragged on for more than twenty days, the city of Jinyong held by Dugu Yongye was never taken, and in the ninth month Gao Anahong brought a relieving army down from Jinyang to Heyang while Zhou Wudi was himself taken ill. Northern Zhou therefore gave up the more than thirty places it had already won and marched home, and the results of the campaign stopped at the line of posts around Heyang and Luokou. For Northern Qi this was a mortal but well-timed blow: the floating bridge at Luokou was destroyed, the fords of the Yellow River were in Zhou hands, the connection between Hebei and Luoyang was cut for several months, and the Qi army was forced to draw its main strength out of Jinyang to march to the rescue. For Northern Zhou, though Luoyang was not taken, the campaign proved that advance by several roads and land-and-water movement together could hold down the Qi system of fortified towns, and it showed Zhou Wudi that a northern campaign was workable. The real ending came two years later before the walls of Ye, but the entrance to that war was the Heyin of the autumn of the fourth year of Jiande.
